Creative answers welcomed, if you built something to have the perfect setup, please share :)
How did you make your work station more ergonomic?

If possible, stand. If not, sit on a chair without a back. Place your keyboard (etc) such that your relaxed arms bend at about 90 degrees to hit the keys. Prop your computer monitor up so the top bezel is at eye-level. These can (mostly) be done with careful stacking of boxes and chair elevations.

In practice, strive for a couple of those. People like to stoop over their workstations, and implementing all of them can be tricky.

Anyway, glad you're liking it! First advice: consider getting a "real" pair of shoes instead of white lumps of plastic.

While the c25k is very well made for keeping you safe and injury free, you'll be spending more and more time in those shoes, and a small issue will be magnified many times over as you build more mileage. Maybe its a little seam that rubs the wrong way, or the laces feel funny, or the heel rubs the back of your foot, or they're a little tight on the pinky... any little thing can lead to ouchies that can make running feel less fun if you're hobbling along with blisters on every toe.

Most running stores have pretty awesome return policies, 30/60/90 day no-questions-asked return or exchange policies are a god send, so I would definitely look at investing in getting fitted for fancy pair of shoes. Shoes typically last 300-600 miles, so a single pair during a c25k should definitely carry you though the program a few times over, so it wouldn't feel like a recurring cost too often.

other than shoes... anything is good to wear, cotton can chafe after a longer run (45+ minutes), but I ran my entire high school cross country career wearing nothing but cotton and I never had any issues, so fancy "tech" shirts aren't an absolute necessity.

I'm sure I'm forgetting stuff, but welcome! have fun, and let the running bug bite ;)
